why: The student predicts the effect of a change to the code: replacing the if with a direct boolean assignment. This prediction is correct for this loop because isDone is false until i % 5 == 0 and the loop ends as soon as it becomes true. The answer does not give the output (1 4 7 10) or say when the loop stops.

concepts.quote: isDone = (i % 5 == 0); would do the same as the if
concepts.why: Says that changing the if to a direct assignment keeps the behaviour. That holds here because the loop exits the first time isDone becomes true, so the false values written before then change nothing.
